destinations.name: Copper Coast
destinations.coordinates_source: candidate: Kadina (Wikipedia town point); recentre in pin step

name_evidence.wording: The Copper Coast: Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta (Moonta/Moonta Bay/Port Hughes was SA Top Tourism Town 2021); Wikivoyage covers Moonta and Wallaroo See listings

destinations.description_notes: Mention the towns Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta in the description (wrapper towns merged into their attractions); Wallaroo is also the ferry port to Lower Eyre.

destinations.name: Yorke Peninsula

name_evidence.source: Wikivoyage "Yorke Peninsula and Clare Valley"; yorkepeninsula.com.au; visityorkepeninsula.com.au
name_evidence.wording: Yorke Peninsula, the peninsula-wide tourism name; this destination holds the east, centre and south coast outside the Copper Coast and Innes National Park

destinations.description_notes: Flag for owner: the name overlaps the Copper Coast and Innes NP sub-destinations; if the owner prefers, rename to Southern Yorke Peninsula. Description mentions Ardrossan, Stansbury, Edithburgh, Minlaton, Yorketown towns.

destinations.name: Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park
destinations.coordinates_source: candidate: Wikipedia area point (park centroid); needs the visitor point (visitor centre / campground)

name_evidence.wording: Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park, the headline Yorke attraction (Ethel wreck, lighthouses, surf, walks)

destinations.description_notes: National park with 12 spots; every national park is a destination.

spots.name: Moonta Mines State Heritage Area
spots.bio: Cornish copper-mining site with the Hughes Pump House, Miners Cottage and a museum, where Australia's "Little Cornwall" began.
spots.reason: 3 counted sources, 1729 page views

spots.name: Moonta Bay
spots.bio: Sandy coves, beaches, a jetty and foreshore at the Moonta township, with Rossiters Point Lookout nearby.
spots.reason: Tourism board township page names sandy coves, beaches, jetty, foreshore and Rossiters Point Lookout (Moonta/Moonta Bay/Port Hughes was SA Top Tourism Town 2021); Wikivoyage Moonta covers the same coast. A beach-and-jetty stop of half an hour or more.

spots.name: The Farm Shed Museum and Tourism Centre
spots.bio: National Trust museum in Kadina with the stump-jump plough, Matta House and a miniature train.
spots.reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage region page and yorkepeninsula.com.au (entry about $12) name this National Trust museum in Kadina with the stump-jump plough, Matta House and a miniature train; allow an hour or more.

spots.name: Wallaroo Heritage and Nautical Museum
spots.bio: Museum on Wallaroo's maritime and mining past, also running ghost tours.
spots.reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Wallaroo See entry and yorkepeninsula.com.au; a museum open daily 10-4 with ghost tours.

spots.name: North Beach, Wallaroo
spots.bio: Long swimming beach on the northern edge of Wallaroo, named by tourism sources.
spots.reason: Rule 1-2: both southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au name North Beach; a long swimming beach with a Wikipedia article.

spots.name: Wheal Hughes Copper Mine
spots.bio: Historic copper mine at Moonta with bookable underground tours through a 55 m tunnel.
spots.reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Moonta and the YP region page both name the underground mine tour (55 m tunnel); a bookable, open visit of an hour or more.

spots.name: Splash Town
spots.bio: Free water park at Moonta Bay, a permanent family venue worth an hour or two.
spots.reason: Rule 1-2: southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au both name this free water park at Moonta Bay, a permanent family venue worth an hour.

spots.name: Port Hughes
spots.bio: Seaside township and beach on the Copper Coast just south of Moonta Bay.
spots.reason: 2 counted sources, 3446 page views

spots.name: Copper Rail Trail
spots.bio: Sealed 25 km walking and cycling path along the old railway linking Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta.
spots.reason: 25 km sealed walking and cycling path between Kadina, Wallaroo and Moonta, named by southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au attraction pages (rules 1, 2).

spots.name: Ardrossan Red Cliffs
spots.bio: Red clay cliffs along the shore beside Ardrossan's historic jetty.
spots.reason: 2 counted sources, 5802 page views

spots.name: Troubridge Island
spots.bio: Conservation park island with an 1855 cast-iron lighthouse and keeper's cottage, visited by boat from Edithburgh.
spots.reason: Rule 1/2: three counted sources including parks.sa.gov.au (Troubridge Island Conservation Park) and Wikivoyage Edithburgh: the 1855 cast-iron lighthouse and keepers cottage, visited by boat from Edithburgh (island is the spot, not the boat).

spots.name: Edithburgh Tidal Pool
spots.bio: Tidal sea-water swimming pool set into the cliff at Edithburgh, with change rooms.
spots.reason: Rule 1/2: two counted sources (Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do and yorkepeninsula.com.au); a tidal sea-water swimming pool set into the cliff, with change rooms, free and always open.

spots.name: Edithburgh Jetty
spots.bio: Jetty known for diving and snorkelling among seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons.
spots.reason: Wikivoyage lists it as its own destination (dive site), and the tourism board says it is renowned for diving and snorkelling with seahorses, Port Jackson sharks and leafy sea dragons; a jetty walk and shore dive a visitor goes for.

spots.name: Corny Point Lighthouse
spots.bio: 1882 lighthouse reserve at the peninsula's south-western corner, reached by Lighthouse Road.
spots.reason: Listed as an attraction by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com; an 1882 lighthouse reserve reached by Lighthouse Road with a picnic area and coast to linger on; Wikivoyage names it too. Free, self-guided.

spots.name: Yorketown Pink Lakes
spots.bio: Salt lakes on the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail, with a viewing platform at Pink Lake and a boardwalk at Par Lake.
spots.reason: Tourism board and southaustralia.com name the Yorke Peninsula Salt Lake Trail (self-drive routes, boardwalk at Par Lake, Pink Lake viewing platform, 15 to 90 min). Objection: lake colour varies by season, and it could duplicate a Salt Lake Trail candidate.

spots.name: Wool Bay Jetty and Lime Kilns
spots.bio: Old port jetty and cliff-top lime kilns with a lookout on the coast road.
spots.reason: Tourism board page names the uniquely designed lime kilns on the cliff top and the old port jetty, with a lookout; a free heritage stop on the coast road. Objection: a short stop, one source.

spots.name: Port Victoria
spots.bio: Western-coast town with an 1878 jetty, a maritime museum and a geology trail.
spots.reason: Town with a historic 1878 jetty, Port Victoria Maritime Museum and geology trail; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and southaustralia.com (rules 1, 2).

spots.name: Port Victoria Maritime Museum
spots.bio: 1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the story of the windjammer grain races.
spots.reason: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Victoria page and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (1877 cargo shed by the jetty telling the windjammer grain-race story). Objection: open weekends 2-4 pm only.

spots.name: Minlaton Harry Butler Red Devil Memorial
spots.bio: Free display of the Red Devil monoplane that made the first airmail flight over the sea.
spots.reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Minlaton and the yorkepeninsula.com.au Minlaton page (the only genuine Red Devil monoplane, first airmail over the sea, free display on the edge of town).

spots.name: Port Vincent
spots.bio: Seaside town on the east coast of the Yorke Peninsula with a beach and jetty.
spots.reason: 2 counted sources, 2594 page views

spots.name: Point Turton
spots.bio: 1876 jetty still used by fishers and white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, with boating and diving.
spots.reason: Tourism board page: 1876 jetty (still used by fishers), white beaches on Hardwicke Bay, boating and diving; a second-tier seaside stop. Beach and jetty are one place (Point Turton Beach is a duplicate).

spots.name: Corny Point
spots.bio: Surf breaks and three swimming beaches, with a coastal drive from Corny Point to Berry Bay.
spots.reason: Tourism board page names surf breaks (Rock Pool, Salmon Hole, Daly Head, Berry Bay), three swimming beaches and the Corny Point to Berry Bay coastal drive; visitors beaches stop. Lighthouse is a separate candidate.

spots.name: Black Point
spots.bio: Safe white-sand beach with no rips, good for crabbing and swimming, beside Pine Point.
spots.reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage (own section with Pine Point, "one of the most gorgeous stretches of coastline") and the tourism board page (safe white-sand beach with no rips, crabbing, swimming).

spots.name: Sultana Point
spots.bio: White-sand swimming beach south of Edithburgh, at the end of the mosaic walking trail.
spots.reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Edithburgh Do names it as the swimming beach south of town with white sand and the end of the mosaic walking trail; a second-tier beach stop (COVERAGE.md).

spots.name: Ardrossan Heritage Museum
spots.bio: Museum in the old Smith stump-jump plough factory, with a Zanoni shipwreck display.
spots.reason: Two sources: yorkepeninsula.com.au and visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (in the old Smith stump-jump plough factory, shipwreck Zanoni display, open seven days 10-4).

spots.name: Stansbury Museum
spots.bio: 1878 schoolroom in Stansbury holding farm and industry displays, open only some afternoons.
spots.reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Stansbury See; visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page): 1878 schoolroom with farm and industry displays. Objection: volunteer-run, open Wed and Sun afternoons.

spots.name: Edithburgh Museum
spots.bio: Museum in a former produce store covering the salt industry and shipwrecks, open at weekends.
spots.reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Edithburgh See (adults $3) and the visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (salt industry, shipwrecks, produce-store building). Objection: weekend afternoons only.

spots.name: Bublacowie Military Museum
spots.bio: Private museum with a large WWI, WWII and Vietnam collection and memorial gardens.
spots.reason: Two sources: visityorkepeninsula.com.au museums page (extensive WWI/WWII/Vietnam collection, memorial gardens, tours) and History SA; guided visits last an hour or two. Objection: private museum, open Sun to Tue or by appointment.

spots.name: Cape Spencer Lighthouse
spots.bio: Lighthouse and lookout on Cape Spencer, also the park's whale-watching cliff.
spots.reason: Lighthouse and lookout on Cape Spencer in Innes National Park, named by parks.sa.gov.au and yorkepeninsula.com.au (Cape Spencer Lookout); also the park's whale-watching cliff. One spot with Cape Spencer (duplicate).

spots.name: Pondalowie Bay
spots.bio: Surf beach and campground at the western end of the park.
spots.reason: Surf beach and campground in the park, named by parks.sa.gov.au and yorkepeninsula.com.au; a beach (and Yorke's best-known surf break) is a standard second-tier keep.

spots.name: Ethel Wreck
spots.bio: Remains of the 1904 wreck of the Ethel on Ethel Beach.
spots.reason: Remains of the Ethel (1904) on Ethel Beach in the park, named by parks.sa.gov.au ('Visit... the shipwreck of the Ethel') and yorkepeninsula.com.au (rules 1, 2). Ethel Beach is a duplicate of this.

spots.name: Royston Head
spots.bio: Headland lookout reached by a 4 km return walk with views of the rugged coast.
spots.reason: Headland lookout, 2-hour 4 km return hike with 'amazing views of the rugged peninsula coast' (parks.sa.gov.au); a headland a guide singles out, second tier but real.

spots.name: Stenhouse Bay
spots.bio: Village in the park with the visitor centre, jetty and campground.
spots.reason: Village in Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park with the visitor centre, jetty, campground and whale-watching cliffs; named by yorkepeninsula.com.au and the parks page (rules 1, 2). Stands in for Stenhouse Bay Jetty (duplicate).

spots.name: West Cape Headland Hike
spots.bio: 1 km loop to West Cape lighthouse with 360 degree views.
spots.reason: 30-minute 1 km loop to West Cape lighthouse with 360 degree views, named on parks.sa.gov.au and highlighted by rangers (rules 1, 2).

spots.name: Inneston
spots.bio: Abandoned gypsum township with ruins, interpretive signs and heritage cottages.
spots.reason: Abandoned gypsum township in the park, a named see on the parks.sa.gov.au page (ruins, interpretive signs, heritage cottages); one spot with Inneston Historic Walk (duplicate of this).

spots.name: Stenhouse Bay Lookout Walk
spots.bio: 2 km cliff-top loop with views over Investigator Strait.
spots.reason: parks.sa.gov.au lists it as an easy 1 hour, 2 km cliff-top loop with views over Investigator Strait "among the best in the park"; a distinct walk from the jetty car park.

spots.name: Dolphin Beach
spots.bio: Beach in Innes National Park on the road to Royston Head, named as one to visit in the park.
spots.reason: Named as a beach to visit in Innes National Park by the Tourism Australia G'day Parks guide (and photographed by southaustralia.com); sits on the Royston Head road. Objection: parks.sa.gov.au gives it only a passing mention, so a single guide source.

spots.name: Marion Bay
spots.bio: Seaside village at the entrance to Innes National Park, with a beach and the park gate.
spots.reason: 2 counted sources, 3151 page views

spots.name: Gym Beach Hike
spots.bio: 9.8 km hike through dunes and mallee between Browns Beach and Gym Beach, the longest trail in the park.
spots.reason: Agency-listed 4 hour, 9.8 km hike through dunes and mallee between Browns Beach and Gym Beach; Wikivoyage calls it the longest trail in the park.

spots.name: Thomson-Pfitzner Plaster Trail
spots.bio: 7.6 km hike along the old railway from Inneston to Stenhouse Bay, with interpretive signs.
spots.reason: Agency-listed 3 hour, 7.6 km hike along the old railway from Inneston to Stenhouse Bay with interpretive signs; Wikivoyage lists it too (though calls it the least interesting trail). Objection: overlaps the Inneston ruins, a plain track.

spots.name: Port Broughton
spots.bio: Northern Yorke Peninsula town with a jetty and a shoreline on the Spencer Gulf estuary.
spots.reason: 2 counted sources, 6461 page views

spots.name: Port Broughton Heritage Centre and Museum
spots.bio: Local heritage museum in Port Broughton, open only on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons.
spots.reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage Port Broughton, $7 entry; yorkepeninsula.com.au Port Broughton page); a permanent venue, small hours do not make it an event. Objection: open only Tue and Thu 1-3 pm.

spots.name: Port Wakefield
spots.bio: Gateway town where the road onto the Yorke Peninsula leaves the Adelaide Plains.
spots.reason: 2 counted sources, 6009 page views

spots.name: Walk the Yorke
spots.bio: About 500 km of coastal walking trail around the Yorke Peninsula, in sections.
spots.reason: 3 counted sources, 0 page views

spots.name: Investigator Strait Shipwreck Trail
spots.bio: Heritage trail of interpretive signs at wreck sites around the southern coast from Edithburgh to Innes.
spots.reason: Heritage trail named by the SA government, southaustralia.com and yorkepeninsula.com.au (interpretive signs around the southern coast from Edithburgh to Innes, including the Ethel wreck). Objection: mainly a dive trail, spread over many sites.

merged.reason: town wrapper beside four of its own attractions

merged.name: Dhilba Guuranda-Innes National Park
merged.reason: the park is the destination, not a spot of itself

review.name: Kernewek Lowender
review.reason: 3 counted sources and 1794 views but a biennial Cornish festival is an event, not a permanent place (COVERAGE.md rule 4); mention in the Copper Coast description and best-time text, no spot

standalone_near_destination_notes.reason: about 45 km north of Kadina, beyond the Copper Coast span (60 km, 45 km reach) and a northern Yorke / Barunga West town travellers file separately; over 100 km from Minlaton

standalone_near_destination_notes.spot: Port Broughton Heritage Centre and Museum

standalone_near_destination_notes.reason: gateway on the Adelaide Plains, about 100 km from Kadina and 110 km from Minlaton
about 500 km trail around the whole peninsula, placed once at the midpoint of the route (null pending research), not under one sub-destination
heritage trail of sites from Edithburgh to Innes, belongs to no single base; coordinates null pending research

notes: Yorke Peninsula (tourism-wide name) is placed alongside Copper Coast and Innes NP: spans barely overlap (Copper Coast centre is 100 km from Minlaton). Spot coordinates are left null where only a town or area point exists; every spot is re-pinned with resolve-pin.py. Costs, ticketUrls and costBasis are null and in needs_research.
